comment: Every HTTP route the dashboard issues, and why. Three things read this file, which is why
it exists rather than the URLs being scattered through the components:
1. src/api/client.ts builds its request paths from it, so a route cannot drift out of
this list without the UI breaking loudly.
2. tests/api_contract_test.rs asserts every entry is covered by CONTRACTS, so a route
the dashboard depends on cannot stop being served without a Rust test failing -- on
the default feature set, with no Node and no built bundle.
3. tests/api/test_dashboard.py replays them against a live server.
The list is read-only, except correcting and forgetting your own memories. It contains
GETs, the six POSTs that only read (search, list, graph and recall are POSTs because their
bodies are too structured for a query string), and exactly two writes: POST
/api/v1/memories and DELETE /api/v1/memories/{r}. The memories are the user's own record
of what their agents know about them, and owning that record means being able to correct
and delete it from the console. Tables and records stay read-only:
the_dashboard_declares_no_route_that_writes allows those two by exact method and path and
POST /api/v1/query is deliberately absent: DXQL executes INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and DROP,
so a console for it would make the tables and records writable from here.

routes.why: is this a DXMT server, and is it answering
overview: version, table count, total records, persistence
overview: in-flight operations, WAL frontier, snapshot state
table detail: schema and record count
table detail: index type, resident flag, bytes
the record browser (vectors omitted), and with with_vector the PCA page's sample
one record in full, including the vector used as a query
the search inspector and both searches of every recall probe
BM25 search; degrades when text-bm25 is not compiled in
vector+text fusion; degrades to dense without text-bm25
the visualize page's neighbour-graph layout — the answer instead of the vectors
the Memories page: newest first, by kind, paged; and finding one memory and the ones it replaced, since there is no GET by id
the Memories page's search, the same recall an agent runs; a read with a structured body
WRITE, one of two: correct a memory, as a new one that supersedes it (history kept) or with the same id to fix a typo in place
WRITE, two of two: forget a memory permanently, after a confirmation that names it
